definitions.explanation: A thin layer of suspended water droplets or particles that reduces visibility, lighter than fog. Meteorologically, visibility is reduced to 1-10 km.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}の{靄|もや}が{湖|みずうみ}にかかっている。
examples.english: Morning haze hangs over the lake.

examples.japanese: {靄|もや}が{晴|は}れて{山|やま}が{見|み}えてきた。
examples.english: The haze cleared and the mountain became visible.

examples.japanese: {靄|もや}のかかった{風景|ふうけい}は{幻想的|げんそうてき}だった。

notes:
KANJI: The kanji {靄|もや} is complex and often written in hiragana.

WEATHER DISTINCTIONS:
・{霧|きり} (fog) - visibility less than 1km, thicker than {靄|もや}
・{靄|もや} (haze/mist) - visibility 1-10km
・{霞|かすみ} (haze) - often used poetically, especially for spring haze

METEOROLOGICAL NOTE: In Japanese weather terminology, {靄|もや} specifically refers to reduced visibility between 1-10 km due to water droplets. When visibility drops below 1 km, it becomes {霧|きり} (fog).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{靄|もや}がかかる (haze/mist covers)
・{靄|もや}が{晴|は}れる (haze clears)
・{靄|もや}に{包|つつ}まれる (to be enveloped in mist)
